title: Students wait for A-level, T-level and BTec grades
description: Hundreds of thousands of students in England, Wales and Northern Ireland will receive A-level, T-level and BTec results on Thursday morning.Another re
body: Hundreds of thousands of students in England, Wales and Northern Ireland will receive A-level, T-level and BTec results on Thursday morning.Another record number of students are expected to find out they have secured a place at their first choice of university.The cost of going to university has been in the spotlight this year, with mounting pressure on the government to reform student loan repayments, and there has been a renewed focus on technical education under Prime Minister Andy Burnham.But the chief executive of Universities UK, which represents more than 140 vice-chancellors, urged students to not "let politicians make your decision for you".About 40% of 18-year-olds in England receive A-levels every summer.Around 250,000 grades for vocational and technical qualifications are also expected to be released to students in England, including BTec National, Cambridge Technical, Cambridge Advanced National and T-level results.AS-levels, which will count towards students' final A-level results next summer in Wales and Northern Ireland, will also be released. This year, the pass rate for National 5, Higher and Advanced Higher exams in Scotland rose across the board.And last year, the proportion of students getting top A-level results reached a record high, with 28.3% of all grades across England, Wales and Northern Ireland marked at A* or A.

title: Major Russian grain export terminals hit in Ukraine Black Sea port attack
description: A "massive" Ukrainian drone and missile strike on Russia's port of Novorossiysk has damaged two major grain export terminals and hit the last big Russ
body: A "massive" Ukrainian drone and missile strike on Russia's port of Novorossiysk has damaged two major grain export terminals and hit the last big Russian naval base on the Black Sea, reports say.Three people, including an eight-year-old child, were killed and another 24 injured in the overnight attack, local officials said.Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky said Kyiv had launched rockets, jet and naval drones in a "unique operation" to strike the Russian base, although he did not mention grain terminals being hit.Ukraine's military later said four Russian warships, including two frigates, were hit. Russia has not commented on the issue."The occupying fleet and all the infrastructure that supports it will not be safe as long as Russian aggression continues," Zelensky said in a post on social media. Most of Russia's Black Sea fleet is docked in Novorossiysk - one of the largest ports in Russia - after it was forced to vacate its former home base of Sevastopol, in the Russia-occupied Crimean peninsula, which was too exposed to Ukrainian attacks.A major grain trading company confirmed to Russia's TASS news agency that its terminal had been hit, while another told Reuters and Russian outlet RBK the same. The Russian agriculture ministry announced on Wednesday that it was working to redirect cargo flows to ports in the Baltic and Caspian Seas as well as land routes. It did not make any reference to Ukraine's attacks but said it was "taking into account current logistical constraints".Repeated explosions reportedly rang out over Novorossiysk throughout the night as air defences shot down aerial objects. An emergency situation was declared in the city on Wednesday, after the barrage of drones struck areas around the port and damaged pipelines, suspending water supply for the city. Elsewhere in the region a man was killed by drone debris, regional Governor Veniamin Kondratyev said. Several locations in the surrounding Krasnodar region were also struck by "several hundred drones" overnight, Kondratyev added, with dozens of buildings damaged, including homes. For its part, Moscow launched aerial overnight strikes which killed at least 11 civilians in Ukraine between Tuesday and Wednesday. The majority were killed when Russia hit the southern city of Zaporizhzhia with ballistic missiles and glide bombs.Russian President Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. After a period of relative calm in the Black Sea, over the course of this summer Kyiv and Moscow resumed striking one another's ports and shipping. The last remaining sea route out of Ukraine has been badly affected by several deadly Russian strikes on cargo ships and the port of Odesa, through which Moscow seeks to put off foreign companies from trading with Ukraine. In July, the Ukrainian Agribusiness Club (UCAB) reported a 23% decrease in exports.Meanwhile, Ukraine has grown increasingly adept at carrying out long-range strikes on Russian territory. Its recent attacks on vessels in the eastern Black Sea have disrupted Russia's grain shipments, too.Russia is the world's largest wheat exporter - but according to a Moscow-based analytics company, exports for August could fall by more than half compared to the same month over the last five years due to the disruption in the Black and Azov seas.On Wednesday, Russian foreign ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova accused Ukraine of carrying out strikes on Russian grain and agricultural infrastructure, resulting in a hike in global food prices and growing grain shortages.But Zakharova also said that Russia would continue striking "facilities that [Ukraine's armed forces] use on the Black Sea to destabilise the navigation situation" until "the full elimination of threats to security projected to the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea".Concerns over how the war in Ukraine would affect global food supplies have been persistent since the start of Russia's invasion in 2022.Together, Russia and Ukraine account for a significant share of global grain trade, particularly for buyers in North Africa, the Middle East and parts of Asia.The 2022 Black Sea Grain Initiative, under which Russia agreed to lift its blockade on Ukraine's agricultural exports, did not last after Moscow resumed attacks on vessels using the maritime corridors to Odesa the following year.

title: How to get a good night's sleep during hot weather
description: Image source, Getty ImagesUpdated 25 June 2026A period of extreme heat across the UK this week has broken records for the hottest day and night temper
body: Image source, Getty ImagesUpdated 25 June 2026A period of extreme heat across the UK this week has broken records for the hottest day and night temperatures ever recorded in June.It can be hard to sleep during periods of hot weather, but these simple tips could help. 1. Don't let yourself napHot weather can make you feel tired and lethargic during the day. That is because you are using more energy to regulate your internal temperature.But if your sleep is disturbed at night, try to avoid napping during the day. When it is hot, feeling sleepy can be precious - save it for bedtime.2. Keep to your normal routinesHot weather can encourage you to change your habits. Don't. That can disrupt your sleep patterns. Try to keep to your usual bedtime routine, and do the things you normally do before bed.3. Remember the basicsTake steps to make sure your bedroom is as cool as it can be at night.During the day, close the curtains or blinds to keep out the sun. Make sure you shut the windows on the sunny side of your home, to keep out hot air.Open all the windows before you go to bed, to get a through breeze.4. Use thin sheetsReduce your bedding but keep covers handy. Thin cotton sheets will absorb sweat. Wearing loose-fitting clothes made of natural fibres like cotton or linen can keep you cooler than sleeping naked. However hot it is in your bedroom, your body temperature will fall during the night. That is why you sometimes wake up feeling cold even though the temperature is higher than usual. 5. Use a fan and chill your socksUsing even a small fan can be sensible in hot weather, especially when it is humid.It encourages the evaporation of sweat and makes it easier for your body to regulate your internal temperature.If you don't have a fan, try filling a hot water bottle with ice cold liquid instead.Alternatively, cool socks in the fridge and put those on. Cooling your feet lowers the overall temperature of your skin and body.6. Stay hydratedYou should make sure you drink enough water throughout the day but should avoid drinking very large amounts before bed.Image source, Getty ImagesIt's about striking the right balance. You don't want to wake up thirsty - but you don't want to have to take an additional trip to the bathroom in the early hours either.7. But think about what you drinkBe careful about soft drinks. Many contain large amounts of caffeine, which stimulates the central nervous system and makes you feel more awake.Avoid drinking too much alcohol as well. Many people drink more when the weather is hot.Alcohol might help you fall asleep but it also promotes early morning waking and a poorer quality of sleep overall.8. Stay calm - and leave your phone aloneIf you are struggling to sleep, get up and do something calming. Try reading, writing, or even folding your washing.But avoid using your phone. Mindless scrolling might seem appealing, but the blue light from the screen can stimulate your brain and leave you feeling more awake. Return to bed when you feel sleepy.9. Keep to the usual bath and bed times for childrenChildren are often quite robust sleepers - but they can be very sensitive to changes in family "mood" and routine.Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Lukewarm baths can help before bedtime during hot weatherMake sure usual bedtimes and bath times do not go out of the window just because it is warm.As part of the bedtime routine, the NHS UK website, external recommends lukewarm baths. Make sure they are not too cold, as that will boost your child's circulation which could increase their temperature.A baby cannot let you know if they are too hot or too cold, so it is important to monitor their temperature. They generally sleep best when their bedroom temperature is between 16C and 20C - use a room thermometer to check. 10. Remember that you will be OKMost of us need about seven to eight hours of good-quality sleep each night to function properly.Teenagers, children and babies typically need more sleep because they are still growing.But remember that the majority of people can still function well after a night or two of disturbed sleep.Although you might yawn a little more frequently than usual, you will probably be fine.These tips were based on suggestions by Prof Kevin Morgan, former director of the Clinical Sleep Research Unit at Loughborough University, and Lisa Artis, of the Sleep Council. This article was first published in July 2019.

schema.headline: How to get a good night's sleep during hot weather

title: Fan tips: Experts advise how best to use yours during a heatwave
description: No air con? Here's how to get the most out of your electric fan ByEsme Stallardclimate and science reporter and George SandemanStruggling to work and
body: No air con? Here's how to get the most out of your electric fan ByEsme Stallardclimate and science reporter and George SandemanStruggling to work and sleep without air con? Your trusty electric fan could help more than you think - but only if you put it in the right place.During the recent heatwaves, social media was full of advice on how to make your fan work harder - but some of it was conflicting. So, to try to clear up any confusion, we asked experts to separate fact from fiction - from which part of your body to direct your electric fan at, to the best room in the house to put it. Keep windows open or closed? The first thing most people will want to know is if opening a window and using a fan at the same time will cool down their home.It depends, says Becci Taylor, a specialist in building physics at the engineering firm Arup.She says it's best to try to keep the air in your home as cool as possible, so you should keep the windows closed during the daytime, when temperatures outside are likely to be at their highest.She recommends drawing curtains and blinds in rooms facing direct sunlight to stop the air inside heating up. "If the air is cooler than your skin temperature, it's going to cool you down even without sweating," she says.You could place a fan in the coldest room and use that to direct its air towards the rest of your home. Though she advises only doing so if you have a reasonably large or powerful fan.If you have a small fan, then it doesn't particularly matter where in the room you place it on a hot day, says Taylor - provided you keep your windows shut. "You just want it to be near you."At night-time, when the air outside is likely cooler than the air in your home, you should consider opening a window and using a fan to bring in the cooler air.Placing the fan next to the open window and pointing it inwards, towards the rest of the room, can help.But pointing the fan towards the window - to try and blow the hot air in your home outwards, as some social media posts advise - isn't particularly useful as you would not get the cooling benefits of having it pointed towards you.Body or face? Where you should point itPointing the fan directly at your face may be tempting during periods of extreme heat, says Prof Mike Tipton from the University of Portsmouth. But he says that will only give you the perception of "thermal comfort" - in other words you will feel cooler but you're not actually cooling as much as you might think.A specialist in human and applied physiology, he says a fan should be directed more broadly at your body and, crucially, placed far enough away so it "provides air movement over the [whole] body".That air movement improves the effectiveness of your sweating, he says, which is caused by your body naturally trying to cool itself down.Using a fan this way works particularly well if you combine it with other methods of keeping your body temperature down, adds Prof Tipton, such as keeping your hands cool and taking tepid showers.However, if you have young children, you should not point a fan directly at them as it could cause dehydration. Instead, you can use the fan to circulate air around the room.Now for an icy blast Putting a bowl of water or ice in front of a fan will also help, Taylor says. That's because the air movement encourages water in the bowl to evaporate, which takes heat out of the air, making the room a little cooler.You can buy fans that come with a misting device, she adds. Taylor says smaller, handheld versions are most effective indoors.Too much mist increases humidity, which reduces your body's ability to sweat and cool down as there's more moisture in the air. Buying a version that is too large means "you just end up with a very sweaty, damp room", she says."Sweating and misting work in the same way, which is also why it's comfortable and cooler to be near a fountain or open body of water," she says."You can harness that mechanism by putting some liquid in front of the fan, which can evaporate."One important tip is never cover your fan with a wet or frozen towel to try and achieve the same effect, as some social media posts demonstrate, as it can cause electrical safety problems.The 35C debateYour body's temperature is about 37C, while your skin is likely to be about 34C.When the air temperature in your home is less than this a fan is helping you sweat, feel cooler and take away heat from the skin.As the air temperature moves above this, Taylor says a fan can still help to evaporate your sweat - as long as it is not too humid - but it will also bring more heat to your skin.The government advice is not to use a fan once it exceeds 35C inside.Met Office scientists have said there is an increasing likelihood of extreme temperatures in the UK, and that the chance of exceeding 40C is accelerating.Taylor adds: "If people can understand how the physiology of cooling works, then we can start to help them deal with the heat better."Illustrations by Jodi Lai.

title: The town making missiles for Trump
description: 'If you're not conservative, don't come here': The town making missiles for TrumpFigure caption, ‘Justified’ or 'no business being there’? Tennessee m
body: 'If you're not conservative, don't come here': The town making missiles for TrumpFigure caption, ‘Justified’ or 'no business being there’? Tennessee munitions town loyal to Trump but divided on IranBySheila FlynnSenior US Reporter, Kingsport, TennesseeAs one local puts it, there's a "church on every street" of the Appalchian community of Kingsport, in the US state of Tennessee.Christianity reigns supreme in this working-class area. Above downtown's historic Lamplight Theatre, a sign proclaims "Jesus first in all things".And while more than 300 area churches may be providing spiritual sustenance to this town of 58,000 people, there's another institution that supplies it with economic nourishment.The Holston Army Ammunition Plant churns out explosives used in Patriot missiles, warheads and other heavy weaponry in the midst of the country's costly and prolonged war with Iran.The war, and its knock-on effects on everything from gas to groceries, has led to a steep decline in President Donald Trump's approval ratings. Recent polling has placed his approval at an historic low of 32% - down 14% from when he first took office in January 2025 - with many Republican respondents citing disillusionment with the president's policies.Image source, Eloise AlannaImage caption, Veteran David Carter, 66, is an outspoken Christian who supports US action in IranThe two big drags on the president's popularity are the cost of living and the Iran War, with one bleeding into the other. The conflict has caused gas prices in the US to spike to above $4 a gallon, a painful hike to any US business that relies on transport.But in Kingsport, support for the president approaches an almost-religious fervor. The city voted overwhelmingly for Trump in all three of his elections. So did wider Tennessee, a Republican state for more than 25 years.When it comes to the Iran conflict, most residents either outright support the military action or rationalise the war's necessity - despite Trump's repeated campaign promise of "no more wars"."If he can stop anyone from having a nuclear bomb, then I'm for it," says Pam Robinson, 65, who spent 20 years working at the local chemical plant.David Carter, a bearded veteran who plays Santa Claus at Christmastime, says "the whole reason we go over there, and we keep everything under control there, is [so that] we don't have it on our doorstep."Others are more blunt."Honestly, I think we should turn them into a parking lot and don't worry about it anymore," says veteran James Camper, 63, wearing a Trump lanyard around his neck as he exits a discount grocery.Veterans account for around 10% of the region's population, and many other households have active duty family members.Robinson, a staunch Christian and independent voter who says her faith informs her candidate choices, believes the remote nature of the war may be preventing local people from being more upset with Trump."Let me say this: If it was hand-to-hand and more people were getting killed, people would be banging the doors down," she says.Image source, Eloise AlannaImage caption, Daniel Overstreet, 53, believes Trump's 'hands are tied' by CongressKingsport's position as a main munitions manufacturer - with Holston standing as the only domestic supplier of some essential explosive and propellant components -  gives its residents a unique perspective when it comes to the war in Iran.The plant employs around 1,000 people and is just one of many sprawling industrial complexes standing out starkly from the lush Appalachian Mountain landscape."The plant's going to be open regardless of whether we're at war or whether we're not," says Daniel Overstreet, 53, standing next to his Harley Davidson in downtown Kingsport. "It is what it is."He believes Trump and the administration are "doing a great job" but there are "too many people trying to fight him.""[He said] he would get the gas prices under control, and they were for a while," says Overstreet. "He said he was gonna get food prices down, but he has no control over that. The president is basically a puppet for Congress and the Senate."His hands are tied, to a certain extent."It's not that people here don't complain about high gas and food prices, inflation and other economic woes - it's just they don't blame Trump for any of it."He's done good on some things; I think he needs to check his advisers and see on some things," says Robinson. "I think he's advised wrong on some things."It was Trump himself, however, who announced his decision to strike Iran in February 2026 following failed negotiations. In an eight-minute video posted to social media, he said "the objective is to defend the American people by eliminating imminent threats from the Iranian regime" - and claimed Iran "will never have a nuclear weapon".Image source, Eloise AlannaImage caption, Evangelist William Bogle believes Trump is 'imperfect' but was the best 'alternative'Evangelist William Bogle, 75, voted for Trump every time he ran and believes the president is "doing a good job" - even though his wife "has to stretch a grocery dollar until, you know, it's big as a bedsheet".Trump is "just gonna have to do a little bit better in some things than he's doing right now," he says."I know he wants the country to prosper."This stalwart support reflects a deeper truth sometimes hidden in the polling headlines. Although Trump has lost favour among more traditional Republicans and independent voters, his base - who self-identify with his "Make America Great Again" mantra - remains much more steadfast in backing him.So while much of the US watches to see how much Trump's sliding popularity may damage Republicans in November's midterm elections, here in the Bible Belt, sometimes red is the only option.As voters turned out last week for local elections, the ballot included a single Democratic candidate. Of the county commission's 11 districts, seven featured only Republicans running, with some unopposed.Many say they can't and won't cross party lines for moral reasons, citing abortion as the single biggest deciding factor, with opposition to socialism and "woke" issues too hard for them to ignore.Those fears outweigh any personal criticisms they may have, says David Carter, 66, a grandfather and Christian as well as a veteran.Trump needs to humble himself more, he concedes, but Carter would only consider a candidate who "supports the morals" of the population. That means opposing  abortion, for example.Image source, Eloise AlannaImage caption, Democrat Adam Teague points out 'there's a church on every street' in KingsportThose who hold more liberal views exist in Kingsport, but they're vastly in the minority and less vocal.Piercing artist Adam Teague, 44, is a gay, heavily-tattooed Democrat working in downtown Kingsport."Before Trump took office, I was wearing, like, rainbow shirts and everything," says Teague, who was raised Baptist. "I kind of toned it down, just to feel safer."Trump was triumphant in the 2024 election in part because of his ability to attract a diverse coalition including people of all ages and races. But while his Maga supporters are sticking by him, polling suggests that many young people who helped get him over the line against Kamala Harris are now disillusioned.Mary Herron, 21, who is leaving a boutique cupcake shop with two friends, has noticed a difference in attitudes amongst her contemporaries."I am seeing a shift in the support … that's kind of rare around here," says Herron, a student who works part-time. "But I've seen a handful of people who have been like, 'Oh yeah, well, I voted for him, and now I'm not with him anymore'."Image source, Eloise AlannaImage caption, Caden Bayless, Mary Herron and Emily Villalpando are 21-year-old progressivesTrump first entered politics when the women were in middle school, says her friend Emily Villalpando, 21. "So a lot of the people that we grew up with kind of just adopted their parents' views."And so now that we're growing up, we're having more responsibilities," says Villalpando, who's studying biomedical science and wants to be a doctor. "The economy affects us a lot more."The three college students - their friend Caden Bayless makes up the trio - cite women's rights and heavy-handed immigration agents as major concerns, but they are sceptical of major attitude or voting shifts in the region. Bayless said she is hopeful the younger generation can make a change, but "given where we live … it would be a very difficult change."Bogle, summing up the Kingsport region, inadvertently speaks to their fears."We live in a great place, and if you're not conservative, don't come here," the preacher says. "Because you wouldn't be a good fit. But if you're conservative, come here, and we'll embrace you."He'll be praying for Trump, he says, as will the more moderate Robinson."All you can do is pray for your leaders, and God will give you what you want in the end," she says.

schema.headline: The town making missiles for Trump

title: A-level results day for teen fighting wildfires at same time as his exams
description: I've been fighting wildfires while I wait for my A-level resultsImage source, MAWWFRSImage caption, Bobi says studying and working has been busy but a
body: I've been fighting wildfires while I wait for my A-level resultsImage source, MAWWFRSImage caption, Bobi says studying and working has been busy but a "great experience"ByBethan LewisWales family and education correspondent and Lola MayorBBC WalesAn 18-year-old firefighter who combined his A-levels with responding to emergency calls is among thousands of students getting results on Thursday morning.Bobi Jones from Newcastle Emlyn in Carmarthenshire said he felt "quite relaxed" about his grades after having "plenty on my plate" responding to recent wildfires.As well as A-levels, results for AS, BTec and other vocational qualifications will also be published, with many students hoping to progress to university.A-level grades can be shared with students from 08:00 BST but arrangements vary depending on the school or college.Bobi is waiting for results for A-level business and sport, as well as the Welsh Baccalaureate qualification. He said his school, Ysgol Bro Teifi, had been "very flexible", with teachers allowing him to leave class when his work alarm went off as long as he caught up with schoolwork afterwards. "The past few months have been very busy with exams and also the fire brigade. We've been really busy with fires and wildfires," he said.Fortunately the problem has not been as serious as in some areas, but Bobi has been regularly responding to "a few patches of grass going up on fire and just spreading very fast". He is now planning to take on an apprenticeship with a local electrician which he will combine with on-call shifts for Mid and West Wales Fire and Rescue Service.Last year, the proportion of A* grades rose slightly to 10.5%, while 29.5% of results were A or A* which was lower than in 2024.Data shows 32.8% of Welsh 18-year-olds had applied for university places by the end of June - slightly up on last year but lower than figures for other UK nations. Image source, Rosa MacGowanImage caption, Rosa is excited about the next chapter after schoolRosa MacGowan, 18, from Swansea juggled studying four A-levels and the Welsh Baccalaureate alongside her part-time job in the hope of going on to be a doctor.Having spent the summer Interrailing and spending time with friends, she is eager to find out what's next."My first choice is to study medicine at Glasgow uni, and my insurance is pharmacy at Newcastle," she said."I am really excited about either of these options, as they seem like really fun cities, and completely different to Swansea."I think both of these courses should have good career prospects, and lots of interesting opportunities."Rosa said she felt "positive about the future and can't wait for the next chapter"."I am nervous for results day, but I am aware that if it doesn't work out, there's plenty of other options, and I can always go travelling again".Image source, William HopkinsImage caption, William Hopkins has been in the Army cadets for six years and wants a career in the armed forcesWilliam Hopkins has been studying for a BTEC in Uniformed Protective Services, alongside his A-levels and hopes to join the Army after results day."I've enjoyed it, but I've never been really academic and I never really enjoyed school that much," he said."I think I'll still get decent-ish grades but I could have probably done a bit more."I'm looking to go into either the Army or Royal Marines as an officer."William wants to follow in the footsteps of family members by joining the armed forces and some of his friends signed up at 16."They've all gone in younger, but I wanted to have a bit more experience living I guess," he added."I've always enjoyed new things and testing my limits."Even if I don't get into the Army I know I will land on my feet somewhere else."Aiming for a place studying criminology with psychology at the University of the West of England in Bristol, Caitlin Giffard, also from Swansea, needs three Bs.She did well in last year's AS results so feels hopeful."It was a real eye-opener, really, the difference between GCSE and A-level, because I had a lot of friends who did quite well at GCSEs, but then had grades drop at A-level."I think it shows how big the jump was."I felt good about my exams though this year, so I'm hoping for good results."Caitlin said she felt "quite positive "about the future despite the unknown of results day being "a little scary".Results for the Advanced Skills Baccalaureate Wales will also be released on Thursday.Many students will need confirmation of their grades to secure university offers and can usually get updated information about their places, external from 08:00 BST.Image source, Caitlin GiffardImage caption, Caitlin needs three Bs to get on to her chosen university courseThe most popular A-level subjects this year were still mathematics, biology, chemistry and psychology.According to provisional data for summer 2026, the largest proportional decreases in entries compared to 2025 were in computer science (-14.9%), Spanish (-12.9%) and drama and theatre (-8.2%).English language and literature entries increased by 23.3%, Welsh language was up 42.7%, while German, from a small base, increased by 59.4%.Image caption, Bethan Evans says there had been a drop in the number of students progressing to study at A-level "particularly in the years since Covid"Fewer 16-year-olds in Wales have been going on to study A-levels in recent years according to data from Medr, the body which oversees and funds post-16 education.Provisional data for 2025/26 suggested that less than half (49%) of Year 11 students who carry on in education now progress to AS courses, the first year of A-levels, compared with 60% in 2014/15.Figures show a growing proportion are going on to study Level 2 courses, which are equivalent to GCSE, rather than a Level 3 course.Bethan Evans, executive director for regulation and analysis at Medr, said there had been a drop in the number of students progressing to study at A-level "particularly in the years since Covid".Asked whether that was a concern, she said there were "more options available to our young people today than ever before"."More and more people at the age of 16 are choosing to go to study vocational qualifications at further education colleges, for example," she said.  This year's results come after a major UK government report, external highlighted "shrinking" job and career opportunities for a "lost generation" of young people with high numbers not in education, employment and training (Neet).Welsh government data suggests that 17% of Welsh young people aged 16 to 24 are Neet.Evans said it was "a significant challenge for us" which had "an impact on people's life prospects". She said Medr worked across universities, colleges and apprenticeship providers to try to address the issue."I think we do see that there is a risk of losing some learners fairly early on in their [education] journey, and that's part of the reason why Medr has put in place an expansion of the junior apprenticeship scheme," she added.

title: Lionel Messi: The Argentine's most iconic moments as he ponders retirement
description: Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, The World Cup success in 2022 was Messi's greatest moment of an amazing career ByEmlyn BegleyBBC Sport journa
body: Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, The World Cup success in 2022 was Messi's greatest moment of an amazing career ByEmlyn BegleyBBC Sport journalistLionel Messi is considering his future in football after the death of his father, Jorge.The 39-year-old Argentina forward is signed with Inter Miami until 2028.But, in an emotional tribute to his dad, he hinted at retirement as he said: "I don't know how to carry on. I used to just play football, and now I'm really not sure if I'll carry on doing it for much longer."He has scored a combined 921 goals for Barcelona, Paris St-Germain, Inter Miami and Argentina.BBC Sport looks at some of the most iconic moments of his remarkable career.First hat-trick as teenager shows talentImage source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Messi scored three Clasico equalisers for his first hat-trickMessi's first career hat-trick came in one of the biggest fixtures in football - El Clasico. At the age of 19, he scored all of Barcelona's goals in a 3-3 draw against rivals Real Madrid on 10 March 2007 - his first at the Camp Nou - including a brilliant last-minute finish after beating a couple of defenders.This was arguably the moment he became a household name.Sublime solo strike sparks Maradona memoriesImage source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Messi has scored many outstanding goals but probably none as good as his dribble and finish against GetafeJust over a month after that hat-trick, Messi scored a goal he has probably never surpassed in the rest of his glorious career.It came in a 5-2 win over Getafe in the Copa del Rey semi-final first leg on 18 April 2007.In a strike with remarkable similarities to compatriot Diego Maradona's (non-handball) effort against England in the 1986 World Cup, Messi picked the ball up in his own half, beat about five defenders, went around the goalkeeper and slotted home.First Champions League final goalImage source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Messi did not score many headers - but he picked a good occasion to net one in the 2009 Champions League final against Manchester UnitedRidiculous as it sounds now, back in 2009 some English football fans and journalists questioned whether Messi could do it against English opponents in Europe - having failed to net in 10 Champions League appearances against Premier League sides.But there were no more doubts when Messi rose highest in the box to head home Xavi's cross in his first Champions League final against Manchester United - and the first game billed as Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo.Two years later he would score in another final win over Sir Alex Ferguson's men to claim the third of his four Champions League winners' medals.Hitting four past ArsenalImage source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Messi scored four or more goals on seven different occasions for BarcelonaMessi scored four goals for the first time in his career as he took Arsenal to the cleaners in the 2010 Champions League quarter-final for a 4-1 home-leg win.The pick of the bunch was his chip over keeper Manuel Almunia to complete his hat-trick.An honourable mention goes to his five-goal haul two years later against Bayer Leverkusen in a 7-1 last-16 success.He is the second top scorer in Champions League history with 129, behind Ronaldo.Breaking Barcelona's scoring recordImage source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Messi is 446 goals clear of anyone else in Barcelona's scoring chartsMessi broke Barcelona's goalscoring record - aged just 24 - in some style with a hat-trick in a 5-3 victory over Granada on 20 March 2012.He equalled Cesar Rodriguez's 60-year-old record of 232 goals with his first, broke it with his second and extended the record with a third.By the time he left Barcelona in 2021 he had extended that mark to 672 goals.A record 91 goals in a yearImage source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Messi scored 1.3 goals per game in 2012A stat so amazing you have to go back to double check to make sure it really happened.In 2012 Messi hit his 91st goal of the year in Barcelona's 3-1 win at Real Valladolid on 22 December.It earned him a place in the Guinness Book of Records., externalHe netted 79 goals for Barcelona and 12 for Argentina - in a total of 69 games for club and country.It was enough to earn Messi a then-unprecedented fourth consecutive Ballon d'Or - even though he only won the Copa del Rey in 2012 for all those goals.New La Liga scoring recordImage source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Messi broke the La Liga scoring record - and would go on to hit more than 200 further Spanish top-flight goalsThis was the second major record Messi broke with a hat-trick.He hit three in a 5-1 win over Sevilla on 22 November 2014 to become the top scorer in La Liga's history.Messi equalled Telmo Zarra's 251-goal mark - set in 1955 by the Athletic Club forward - with a free-kick, before breaking it and stretching it with a third.He ended up on 474 goals, far clear of Ronaldo's 311 for Real Madrid.A 500th Barcelona goal - and in another El ClasicoImage source, Getty ImagesImage caption, This was one of Messi's most famous celebrationsAll the narratives seemed to come together in Barcelona's 3-2 win at Real Madrid on 23 April 2017.Messi popped up with an injury-time goal, sweeping home a first-time shot from the edge of the area. It was an El Clasico winner, his 500th Barcelona goal and it sent his side top of the table - although Real would go on to win the league at the end of that season.For good measure, he pulled out an iconic celebration when he took off his shirt and held it out so the Bernabeu faithful could see his name.Tears at end of 21-year Barcelona stayFigure caption, Lionel Messi in tears as he receives ovation from FC Barcelona at press conferenceThe almost unthinkable happened in August 2021 as Messi left Barcelona on a free transfer.After 21 years, 672 goals and 35 trophies, he had to leave because the club could not afford to honour the new contract they agreed because of La Liga's salary limit.In an emotional news conference, a tearful Messi said: "My family and I were convinced we were going to stay here, at home."I don't want to leave this club - it's a club I love and this is a moment I didn't expect."Despite being linked with Manchester City, he joined Paris St-Germain.First international trophy with ArgentinaImage source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Messi has won three major internatioanl trophies - all after the age of 34On 11 July, 2021, Messi - at the age of 34 - won his first senior international trophy as Argentina beat Brazil 1-0 in the Copa America final at the Maracana.He was named player of the tournament after scoring four goals.An emotional Messi fell to the ground as the full-time whistle blew and was thrown in the air by his team-mates as they celebrated.He won his second Copa America three years later.World Cup triumph & best player awardImage source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Messi finally won the World Cup in 2022 - and was named the tournament's best playerIt was a triumph and moment that looked like it would never happen, with Messi having previously retired from international football before coming back.It was always the thing held against him in debates about whether he was the greatest footballer of all time.Messi scored two goals, and his effort in the 2022 shootout, as Argentina beat France on penalties after a 3-3 draw in the best World Cup final ever.He was named player of the tournament, having netted seven times - including efforts in each knockout round.A record eighth Ballon d'OrImage source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Messi was an Inter Miami player when he won his last Ballon d'OrMessi won another two Ballons d'Or after leaving Barcelona - one at Paris St-Germain and one at Inter Miami - to extend his record haul to eight.His last one came in October 2023 after he won the World Cup and helped his Major League Soccer side lift the Leagues Cup for their first trophy."I couldn't imagine having the career I've had and everything I've achieved, the fortune I've had to be part of the best team in history," he said."All of them [Ballon d'Or awards] are special for different reasons."The World Cup's top scorer - albeit brieflyImage source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Messi played a key role in Argentina's World Cup semi-final win against EnglandIf 2026 was to be his last World Cup, Messi certainly went out in style.His eight goals in the tournament took him 21 in the World Cup - more than anyone has ever scored, until Mbappe went past that tally to 22 in the Bronze Final defeat by England.Aged 39, Messi's World Cup may have ended in disappointment - as Argentina lost to Spain in the final - but individually it was another month on football's biggest stage few will forget.

schema.headline: Lionel Messi: The Argentine's most iconic moments as he ponders retirement

title: Trump says Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt to leave post
description: Leavitt has had a sometimes combative relationship with the media during her tenure, accusing some reporters of being biased or left-wing.In February
body: Leavitt has had a sometimes combative relationship with the media during her tenure, accusing some reporters of being biased or left-wing.In February last year, her office seized control of the White House press pool, stripping organisational duties from the White House Correspondent's Association, as well as initially barring the Associated Press over its refusal to adopt the term "Gulf of America".Among supporters of the Trump administration, however, she was widely praised for remaining "on message" and ferociously defending the president's policies."Watching it in person was even better than watching it online," Fox host and conservative activist Riley Gaines wrote on X after one particularly feisty briefing room exchange. "Karoline Leavitt is so good at her job."She is the second longest-serving press secretary in either of Trump's administrations, following only Sarah Huckabee Sanders.It is unclear who will now become Trump's sixth chief spokesperson across his two administrations.During Leavitt's roughly seven-week maternity leave earlier this year, a series of senior Trump administration figures took the podium including Vice-President JD Vance, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and Secretary of the Interior Doug Bergum.The BBC has contacted the White House for comment on potential choices and the timeline of her replacement's selection.In an interview with Fox News on Wednesday, White House Deputy Chief of Staff Stephen Miller - who called Leavitt a "close friend" and "role model"."We're going to continue working together every single day," he added. "Her story is just beginning. I can't wait to see what her future holds."

schema.headline: Trump says Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt to leave post

title: Lucy Davis: Comedian Jasper Carrott says he is 'so proud' of daughter following her cancer diagnosis
description: Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Jasper Carrott thanked the public "for the love and concern" shown to daughter Lucy DavisBySteven McIntoshEnt
body: Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Jasper Carrott thanked the public "for the love and concern" shown to daughter Lucy DavisBySteven McIntoshEntertainment reporter Actor and comedian Jasper Carrott has spoken about his pride and love for daughter Lucy Davis after she announced she has incurable breast cancer.The actress, best known for playing receptionist Dawn Tinsley in BBC sitcom The Office, has received an outpouring of support since she revealed her diagnosis on Tuesday.Carrott, who was one of the most familiar faces on British television over several decades, told BBC News: "This is a very difficult time for the whole family and we have been supporting her in every way possible since her diagnosis."We are so grateful for all the support we have had over this trying time and we are very hopeful for her future being what she wants it to be."He added: "We are so proud of our daughter and love her so much. The way she has conducted herself through many traumatic health issues is a lesson to us all."We would request privacy for the coming months, but thanks once again for the love and concern shown by so many people."Carrott, whose real name is Robert Davis, became a household name in the 1970s thanks to his stand-up comedy and novelty songs.He has presented programmes such as Canned Carrott, Golden Balls and Carrott's Commercial Breakdown, and acted in comedy series such as The Detectives.Image caption, The Office starred Mackenzie Crook, Ricky Gervais, Lucy Davis and Martin FreemanIn a statement on Instagram on Tuesday, Davis explained: "A year-and-a-half ago I was diagnosed with stage four breast cancer, which has metastasised to my bones. "Specifically to my spine, right hip, and my ribs. The cancer is incurable, and too late for chemo."The initial lump that I felt, wasn't a 'lump' as such; rather a kind of hard spot. Really tiny. I almost didn't bother getting it checked. So I guess I'm saying don't ignore anything - get everything checked out."She added: "As of now, I'm trying to live out whatever might be left of my life in as fun a way as I possibly can... I'm not scared of whatever comes next. I'm at peace with it."As well as The Office, Davis has appeared in Shaun of the Dead, Wonder Woman, The Chilling Adventures of Sabrina, Studio 60 on the Sunset Strip and BBC Radio 4's The Archers.'You are full of magic'After posting her statement, Davis received support from her Office co-stars including creator Ricky Gervais.Actress Jenna Fischer, who played the same role as Davis in the US version of the sitcom, wrote: "Beautiful post. Love you lots."US actress Sarah Paulson, who appeared opposite Davis in Studio 60, said: "Sending you love love love, you are and always have been full of magic."Other stars sending support included Ulrika Jonsson, Amanda Abbington, Edgar Wright, Piers Morgan and Sir Chris Hoy, the Olympic cycling champion who was diagnosed with stage four prostate cancer, who wrote: "Keep going Lucy."According to Cancer Research UK,, external stage four breast cancer is a cancer that starts in the breast tissue but spreads to another part of the body, making it incurable. Treatment can control the cancer for some years, however.The main symptoms of breast cancer in women may include a lump, or swelling in your breast, chest or armpit, the NHS website says., externalSymptoms can also include a change in the skin of your breast such as dimpling or redness, a change in size or shape of one or both breasts, and/or nipple discharge (if you are not pregnant or breastfeeding), which may have blood in it.Other symptoms may include a change in the shape or look of the nipple, such as it turning inwards or a rash on it.

schema.headline: Lucy Davis: Comedian Jasper Carrott says he is 'so proud' of daughter following her cancer diagnosis

title: Travis Kelce shares first comments about wedding to Taylor Swift - 'Best night of my life'
description: American football player Travis Kelce has reflected on his wedding to Taylor Swift, telling US media that their nuptials were "the best night of my li
body: American football player Travis Kelce has reflected on his wedding to Taylor Swift, telling US media that their nuptials were "the best night of my life".Kelce and Swift tied the knot on 3 July at New York's Madison Square Garden in a star-studded event that was largely kept private.Few details from the ceremony have been shared publicly and Kelce's comments on Wednesday mark the first he's shared since the couple were wed by comedic actor Adam Sandler."It was kind of cool to live out my childhood dream of being in that venue, the mecca of all sports venues, being able to get married there," Kelce told reporters at the Kansas City Chiefs' training camp in Missouri.Kelce called the wedding "the best night of my life", thanking guests who attended and calling it "a crazy night". The NFL star and the award-winning singer have kept much of the details of the wedding private and there have been no official photos released of the ceremony held inside the stadium. A litany of Hollywood A-list stars, such as actors Hugh Grant and Jason Sudeikis, singer Benson Boone and model Gigi Hadid were in attendance. Kelce said he had wanted to attend a game when the New York Knicks basketball team were having a good playoff run last year, but had other commitments. The team ended up winning the NBA championships for the first time in nearly six decades."My wife went when I was stuck in a mini camp so I didn't get my opportunity to go then," he said referring to Swift as his wife publicly for the first time. She sat courtside at Game 4 of the NBA Finals, when the Knicks pulled off a stunning upset against the San Antonio Spurs in a 107-106 finish.

schema.headline: Travis Kelce shares first comments about wedding to Taylor Swift - 'Best night of my life'

title: Woman pulled alive from rubble 36 hours after Colombia quake
description: A 32-year-old woman, who had been trapped under rubble for 36 hours following the 7.4-magnitude quake which shook western Colombia, has been rescued a
body: A 32-year-old woman, who had been trapped under rubble for 36 hours following the 7.4-magnitude quake which shook western Colombia, has been rescued alive.Daniela Largo was pulled from beneath a collapsed building in the city of Pereira after a 10-hour-long rescue operation. Firefighters finally managed to reach her via a tunnel they dug below four concrete slabs under which she had been buried.At least 265 people have died in the quake, according to Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella, who said that 496 others remain missing. In Pereira, a city in Colombia's coffee-growing region, 79 people are confirmed to have died, the second-highest number after Cali, where 95 are dead, according to figures by the Association of Colombian Capital Cities (Asocapitales).Largo's mother told AFP news agency that a local resident had heard her daughter cry out for help from beneath the rubble.Once emergency workers had arrived at the site, they were able to locate Largo with the help of a small camera.However, her rescue was complicated by the fact that four heavy concrete slabs were blocking the way.Local firefighters aided by colleagues deployed from the capital, Bogotá, and the disaster response team of the national police force had to dig two tunnels to reach her. Through one opening, dug from above, they were able to provide Largo with oxygen. But it was only through a second tunnel, dug from below, that they were able to free her. De la Espriella celebrated her rescue on social media, describing it as "news which fills us with hope".Largo's mother said that "at home, her 12-year-old son is waiting for her".In Pereira, at least 92 buildings collapsed. Fifteen people are known to be trapped and another 37 have been reported missing, according to Asocapitales. In Cali, Colombia's third most populous city, more than 200 people remained trapped as of 16:00 local time on Tuesday.

schema.headline: Woman pulled alive from rubble 36 hours after Colombia quake

title: Eurovision Song Contest changes rules for countries at war
description: Organisers of the Eurovision Song Contest have updated their rules to state that if a country involved in an armed conflict wins the competition, it w
body: Organisers of the Eurovision Song Contest have updated their rules to state that if a country involved in an armed conflict wins the competition, it will be ineligible to host it the following year.The amendment was approved by the contest's governing body, following feedback from participating broadcasters after Eurovision 2026 in Vienna.It states that winning countries will also be disqualified from hosting if a "sensitive geopolitical situation" affects the "security, safety or stability of their state or immediate region".The update will be interpreted as a reaction to Israel's continued presence at the contest, amid criticism of its military actions in Gaza and the Middle East.Last November, following a failed attempt to have Israel suspended, five broadcasters announced they were boycotting the competition - including Eurovision powerhouses Spain and Ireland.Despite the protests, Israel's Noam Bettan ultimately took second place with his song Michelle. It marked the second year in a row that Israel had taken the runners-up position - and some participating broadcasters have privately expressed safety concerns over the contest being staged in Jerusalem or Tel Aviv, should the country win in the future.Although Israel will undoubtedly be seen as the target of the rule change, it will also affect Ukraine, which has been engaged in a protracted war since it was invaded by Russia in 2022.Ukrainian group Kalush Orchestra went on to win Eurovision that same year, in a symbolic show of public support.Following their victory, Eurovision organisers undertook a "full assessment and feasibility study" to decide whether the 2023 contest could proceed in Kyiv.They ultimately decided the security risks were too great, and the UK stepped in to host the competition in Liverpool.Other rules announced on Tuesday raised the minimum age for participation in Eurovision from 16 to 18; and clarified regulations on the use of backing tracks.Since 1999, live instruments have effectively been banned, with only the lead vocalist performing live. From next year's contest, the backing track may not "unduly assist" the singer or singers on stage, for example by including a pre-recorded voice singing the main melody to thicken or support the live performance."The clarification is intended to protect the integrity of each performance and to ensure the audience always hears the lead vocals on each song performed live," said the EBU.Commenting on the updated rules, Eurovision director Martin Green said: "These changes are about giving everyone involved greater clarity, protecting artists and ensuring the Contest continues to provide a safe and welcoming environment, while preserving the spirit and integrity that make the Eurovision Song Contest so special."Next year's contest will be held in Bulgaria, after their entrant Dara won the 2026 edition with her club anthem Bangaranga.Last month, it was announced that Canada would enter the contest for the first time.

schema.headline: Eurovision Song Contest changes rules for countries at war

title: How do I apply for an apprenticeship and what will I get paid?
description: Image source, Getty ImagesByEducation correspondentUpdated 9 hours agoApprenticeships offer an route into work and further qualifications for people w
body: Image source, Getty ImagesByEducation correspondentUpdated 9 hours agoApprenticeships offer an route into work and further qualifications for people who want to learn while earning.But what is an apprenticeship, how much do apprentices get paid and what careers can they lead to?What is an apprenticeship and what job could I get?An apprenticeship combines paid work with study towards a recognised qualification.Apprentices usually spend most of their time working and part of their time completing training with an employer, college, university or online provider.People often choose apprenticeships because they know the career they want to pursue, or because they want to gain new skills without studying full-time.Any employer can hire apprentices. They are responsible for ensuring apprentices work with experienced staff and receive time away from their job to complete their studying.Apprenticeships are available across a wide range of industries, including business, engineering, construction, healthcare, digital, hospitality and creative sectors.How much are apprentices paid?You get paid for the time you spend working.If you are under 19, or if you are 19 or older but in the first year of your apprenticeship, you will be paid at least the apprentice rate, external of £8 per hour. Those over 19 - or who have already completed their first year - are entitled to the appropriate minimum wage for their age:£10.85 for 19 and 20-year-olds£12.71 for those aged 21 or aboveThese rates apply across the UK but employers can choose to pay more than the legal minimum.Some apprenticeships can also lead to higher salaries after completion.What are the different levels of apprenticeship?In England, Wales and Northern Ireland, the different levels of apprenticeship are:Intermediate (Level 2 - GCSE standard)Advanced (Level 3 - A-level standard)Higher (Levels 4, 5, 6 and 7 - foundation degree or above)Degree (Levels 6 and 7 - bachelor's or master's degree)In Scotland, the different levels are:Foundation (mostly SCQF Level 6 - Highers standard)Modern (mostly SCQF Levels 6 and 7 - Highers or Advanced Highers standard)Graduate (SCQF Levels 9, 10 and 11 - undergraduate or master's degree standard)Advanced apprenticeships - A-level standard - are the most popular, and the number of people doing higher apprenticeships has been rising.How many people do apprenticeships and what could change?Hundreds of thousands of people are on apprenticeships in England each year.Apprenticeships are available for school leavers, young people and adults looking to develop new skills or change careers.The government has introduced a number of measures aimed at increasing apprenticeship opportunities and helping more young people access training.There have also been concerns about the decline in the number of young people starting apprenticeships in recent years, as well as whether opportunities are equally accessible to people from different backgrounds.How do you find an apprenticeship?If you know where you want to work, you can head straight to the employer's website and apply.You can search for apprenticeship opportunities through different official websites in England, external, Scotland, external, Wales, external or Northern Ireland, external. The Universities and Colleges Admissions Service (Ucas) website, external also lets you search for apprenticeship vacancies. You will be interviewed for the apprenticeship before you start, and will need to pass an assessment showing what you have learned before you can finish.Think hard about what the apprenticeship offers. Can you picture yourself in a job in the industry? Will the qualification help you in the career? What opportunities exist at the organisation itself?Make sure you understand what training you will receive, how much you will get paid, and how long the placement will last. You can also read reviews of apprenticeships on sites such as RateMyApprenticeship.co.uk., externalWhat are some of the problems with apprenticeships?Some apprentices do not complete their training.Reasons for leaving early can include personal circumstances, changing career plans, problems with the quality of training or not receiving enough time to study.Ucas has previously warned that young people were being put off by a range of barriers, including:low paylack of availabilityhaving to apply for apprenticeships individuallyThe government has introduced changes to apprenticeship rules in England, including reforms to course requirements, as it tries to increase the number of opportunities available.

schema.headline: How do I apply for an apprenticeship and what will I get paid?

title: ICE equipping agents with gloves that deliver electric shocks
description: Unlike a taser, which uses sharp barbs in the skin to deliver a shock of up to 50,000 volts, the gloves do not complete an electrical circuit inside t
body: Unlike a taser, which uses sharp barbs in the skin to deliver a shock of up to 50,000 volts, the gloves do not complete an electrical circuit inside the body.The gloves instead deliver a sharp shock to convince a subject to comply using "pain deterrence", says Lt Butch Gallion, an administrator at Hawkins County jail in Tennessee."We may or may not deploy them. It just depends on how they act. When you push the button to turn them on there's a light that displays. The inmates understand that light, and often just seeing the light brings compliance," he says.The shocks can only be delivered when they contact skin, allowing an officer to touch a subject's clothing, and then move to the skin – typically the wrist or elbow - if they begin to fight.If they become combative, he continues, "then you can apply the gloves to an area that the skin is exposed. And it's an instant complier for me".According to the DHS note, GLOVE would be used by officers and agents in Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), which targets transnational criminal organisations, and Enforcement Removal Operations (ERO), which is responsible for arresting, detaining and deporting people who violate immigration laws in the US. Some law enforcement agencies are already using the gloves but it's believed that the planned ICE purchase would be the largest from Compliant Technologies to date.  Civil rights groups, including the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU), have expressed alarm about law enforcement using them. "ICE spent the last year showing this country that they are willing to disregard the law and are too quick to use force, with devastating and at times fatal consequences for citizens and noncitizens alike," said Jenn Rolnick Borchetta, deputy director on policing at the ACLU.  Federal immigration agents have been criticised in the wake of fatalities that have occurred during enforcement operations.Recent incidents include the fatal shooting of Mexican national Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Texas, while Colombian national Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero was killed during an immigration enforcement operation in Maine.ICE has also been under pressure to deliver President Donald Trump's deportation agenda, which includes meeting a daily target of arrests."Now they [ICE] might be equipped with a device that allows them to deliver an electric shock with their hands by pushing a small button, in a move that might be imperceptible to those watching," Borchetta said. "Giving immigration agents a concealed means of delivering terrible pain is a recipe for more harm to the public and less accountability."With reporting by Max Matza

schema.headline: ICE equipping agents with gloves that deliver electric shocks
